Commentary.Commentary: Plenty of positives for the women's cricket in India, despite this loss. Priceless, valuable experience to take back home and they've shown the world what they're capable of as well. Right, then. This is where we say goodbye. We hope all of you had a good time and enjoyed this coverage of ours. Like they say - the end of one thing, the beginning of another. There will be plenty more matches to come, see you soon. Cheers!

Even in the face of defeat, they always had that belief, which is why England are deserving winners this evening at Lord's. You don't become champions for the fourth time just by dumb luck, it's their quality and their skills and their determination that has got them here. Can take every joy in lifting that trophy and we're all sure there are plenty of celebrations going deep into the night.

England captain, Heather Knight praises her girls for being outstanding. Adds that all the hard work they did and tight games they won in the last 18 months came in handy today. Credits India for having a brilliant tournament. Feels her teammates held their nerves when the partnerships were going on. Thanks everyone for the support. Adds that women's cricket is growing from strength to strength and all the teams showed that. Believes that England was the best place to host the tournament.

India captain, Mithali Raj says she is proud of her team but credits England for keeping their nerve. Reckons the match was hanging in the balance and the occasion probably got to them. States she is really proud of her girls for putting in such a performance and making it difficult for every opposition they faced. When asked about Jhulan Goswami, exclaims she is an experienced bowler and has delivered whenever required, but says she also kept in mind that England bat deep and are not to be taken lightly. On what was the reason for their loss today, replies that most of the players are young and don't have experience with such things, but this experience will help them in the future. On this being her last World Cup, informs she will play for another couple of years, but this is her last World Cup. Adds that Goswami has done her part for the country and women's cricket in India. Ends by saying that she hopes this changes things and women's cricket is viewed in a different light now.

Player of the Tournament, Tammy Beaumont is all smiles and is thrilled with this victory. Praises all the girls for stepping up in the tournament. Adds that the plan was to see off the early phase as they thought the pitch will do something in the morning. Admits that the middle order collapse didn't help their cause but Gunn and Brunt added useful runs. Further praises all the bowlers. Credits Kaur and Raut for an exceptional partnership but says that she was never in doubt of defending the total in her head. Also adds that it's a great feeling to be playing at Lord's.

Player of the Match, Anya Shrubsole says she can't believe they've won and is lost for words. States it was an amazing team performance to stick in there and find a way to win the game, which is unbelievable. Further states it was important they got everything right, with so much at stake in a World Cup final, so is happy that they ended up on the right side. When asked about the crowd here at Lord's, lets everybody know that the support has been absolutely amazing and mentions that she's never been in a game where the crowd is so loud that you can't hear the player next to you. On what they learned from their tournament opener defeat to India, replies what this team has shown is a huge amount of fight and that's what helped them win the World Cup in the end.

Mark Robinson (coach) feels it was all about picking  one wicket when the partnership (Raut-Kaur) was going on. Feels that they were in the game as the slow bowlers were hard to get away. Adds that it was a great atmosphere today and he really enjoyed every minute and is happy to come out on the right side.

Sarah Taylor is very proud of her teammates. She says that personally it's been a roller-coaster year for her (due to injuries). Jenny Gunn who missed the final in 2009 due to an injury is ecstatic after today's win. Considers this as one of the best teams she has played with. Sarah Taylor praises India for playing exceptionally well and feels they will bounce back in future. A word of praise for skipper Heather Knight and Sarah Taylor terms her a calm character.

Lauren Winfield says that they kept on backing each other in spite of the partnerships. Laura Marsh feels every run was important and they just stuck in there. Laughs and says it sounds amazing to be called - World Champions!

Anya Shrubsole is lost for words after a tremendous performance. Feels it's the fitting finale. Says that they never lost hope and knew a couple of wickets will bring them back in the match. She adds that it's a childhood dream come true for her.

Alex Hartley is thrilled after the win and says that this is what they work hard for. Calls Anya Shrubsole the hero! Fran Wilson praises the character of her teammates and terms Anya Shrubsole's performance as amazing.

But, that's not all where the credit lies. Earlier in the day, fighting knocks from Taylor and Sciver, along with some handy runs from the English middle order saw that there was a challenging score in front of the Women in Blue, something which their bowlers were ultimately able to defend. A collective performance, the way it should be.

Credit must be given to the English women. Despite being second best for a large chunk of the game, they never gave up and kept on fighting. Anya Shrubsole being their lead attacker, with a 6-fer in the final. What a champion! Alex Hartley chipped in with 2 of her own and there were two run outs enforced. A truly amazing, character-filled performance. You'd expect nothing else from the now 4-time world champions.

It seemed like India would take the game after being in control for so long, but their half century stand was broken when Raut was caught leg before. And this is where the game turned on its head. The Indians completely lost the plot from this point on. What we witnessed was a colossal collapse. From 191/3, India got all out for 219 - 28 runs for the loss of 7 wickets. Maybe the pressure got to them and they crumbled under that.

After setting a target of 229 in front of India, England started taking a couple of relatively early wickets. But then Raut and Kaur took the situation in their stride and steadied the ship at first. Kept the scoreboard ticking and made their respective fifties in the process of making a 95-run stand. The latter departed but Raut carried on with Krishnamurthy, who took the attack to the opposition.

ENGLAND ARE THE CHAMPIONS FOR THE FOURTH TIME! Emotions running high on the field as the English players are jumping in joy and hugging each other. The crowd has gone bonkers. What a final! But we must applaud India for the way they fought. Sad faces all around in their camp, tears rolling down but they should be proud of themselves. A match worthy of the finals, went right down to the wire where England held their nerves better than the Indian team.

OUT! ENGLAND ARE THE 2017 WOMEN'S WORLD CUP CHAMPIONS! What a moment for them, their unbeaten finals' record at home remains intact, three in a row now and their fourth title overall. Fittingly, it's Shrubsole who finishes things off for the home side. A very full ball attacking the stumps, Gayakwad cannot keep it out as she is slow to bring her bat down. The woodwork is shattered and that seals the deal. Screams of delight among the fielding side players and their support staff. ENGLAND WIN BY 9 RUNS!

DROPPED BY GUNN! That was almost the Cup, right there. That's a sitter but she has put it down. Fuller ball outside off, Poonam looks to go big down the ground but doesn't get the elevation. It goes to Gunn who spills a dolly at mid off.
Full and outside off, jammed out towards cover. Good shot but cannot find the gap.
Rajeshwari Gayakwad is the last batsman for India.

OUT! GONE! IS THAT THE GAME? England certainly believe so and it's a 5-fer for Shrubsole. Slower ball outside off, Deepti is early into the chip shot and mistimes it horribly. The short mid-wicket fielder Sciver backtracks to her right to take the catch easily. JUST ONE WICKET NEEDED FOR ENGLAND NOW, 11 RUNS NEEDED OFF 11 BALLS.
Full and outside off, drives crisply towards mid off who is at the edge of the circle. Poonam wants the single but Deepti rightfully sends her back. She wants the strike.Wise call!
Very full and around middle, leans across and digs it out past the diving bowler towards mid on. Deepti wants the single but is sent back, puts in a dive to save herself.
Fuller and outside off, leans forward and drives to mid off.
Poonam Yadav is the next batter in. What a moment to walk in. Will she play a part in her team winning the World Cup?

OUT! SUICIDAL RUN AND GONE! India are digging a hole for themselves here. Shortish and outside off, cut towards point and she wanted a single but the partner was never interested. Too late for Shikha to return as the throw at the keeper's end is accurate from Shrubsole. Taylor does the rest and Pandey is well short. 11 OFF 15 NEEDED NOW.
Wide! Fired down the leg side, Pandey misses the flick and it's a wide.
This is good from the Indians. The singles are coming and they can actually afford to do it in ones.
Slower ball outside off, Pandey waits for it and dabs gently to short third man as the batsmen sneak a single. Back to Deepti now.
Jenny Gunn back on. 14 needed from 18. Can she get a wicket here? Or will the rain pouring down hard now come in the way of that?
Length ball around off stump, Pandey pushes at it but gets a thickish inside edge in front of square leg. Single taken. England won't mind this as they have the tailender on strike for the new over.
Length ball around off stump, gets back and taps it gently towards point.
Fullish around off stump, driven down the ground to long on for a single.

NOT OUT! Wide! Sprays one down the leg side, Deepti misses the flick as Taylor whips off the bails in a flash. They go upstairs for the stumping appeal, the England keeper seems very excited. The replays show that it is really touch and go, very, very close and perhaps too narrow to call for the third umpire. The benefit of the doubt goes to the batsman and Deepti survives. India breathe easy. Wide called meanwhile.
Hold on! This could be real close. A stumping appeal against Deepti Sharma is referred by the square leg umpire.
Good running! Length ball around middle, Deepti glances it down to the left of fine leg and the pair scamper back for the second run.
Very full and outside off, Pandey looks to drive but gets a thickish edge down to third man. Single taken. Strike back to Sharma now.
Length ball on middle, worked gently to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Floated on a length outside off, gets back and punches it towards cover.
Floated around middle, steps out and eases it towards long on for a single.
Full and outside off, steps out and digs it out to long off for a single.
Fullish and outside off, steps out and jams it towards short cover.
Skips down the pitch again and eases it to long off for a run.

FOUR! Super shot! Deepti steps out to this and lofts it dead straight down the ground. Safe stroke and it races away to the fence for a boundary. Much-needed one for the Indians. She is absolute key now to this run chase.

Shikha Pandey to bat next. 28 needed from 30. Still not all is lost for India. Deepti Sharma is batting, the equation isn't bad at all. Shikha just needs to keep giving Deepti the strike. But can she?

OUT! KNOCKED HER OVER! Shrubsole is pumped up and so are the English players. The pendulum seems to be swinging, folks. A very full ball around middle, almost a yorker and Jhulan cannot bring her bat down in time. Rattle of timber and she has to make the long walk back to the pavilion. India under tremendous pressure now.
Fullish ball on the pads, gets across and clips it down to fine leg for a single.
Jhulan Goswami is next in to bat.

OUT! Length ball angling into the batsman, Veda attempts to slog it over mid-wicket but gets a big top edge. The ball balloons in the air and Sciver settles underneath it inside the ring. Going right down to the wire. 29 needed off 32 balls.
Switches to around the wicket and angles in a fuller length ball on off, Deepti swings it off the inside half over mid-wicket. Another single taken.

Fuller in length again, around off, Veda winds up for a massive slog across the line but it takes the inner half of the bat and rolls through mid-wicket. They pick up a single. 30 needed off 34 balls!
Fullish and on middle and leg, Veda kneels to attempt the sweep shot but misses. A stifled appeal for an lbw dies down quickly.
Top edge but safe! A touch short and on middle and leg, Krishnamurthy swivels with the pull but mistimes it behind square leg. Falls safely and they take a single.
Dances down the track and drives it to long on for a single.

Not out! Floated full ball on off, Deepti gets forward and pushes it towards point. Miscommunication over a single, pressure telling, both batters in the middle of the pitch and then they decide to return. A direct hit at the striker's end, appeal is made and the square leg umpire goes upstairs. Just safe, Sharma.
A run out appeal against Deepti Sharma is referred upstairs. She looks safe in normal time.

Deepti Sharma is next in. Walking in a high pressure situation. 33 needed off 39. This 19-year old is known to have a calm head over her shoulders, despite her age. This will be a true test of her character.

OUT! Bowled! This is getting very interesting, folks. Hartley tosses it up in the air and lands it full around leg, Verma gets down and across for the sweep shot but misses. It kisses her gloves and goes behind to disturb the stumps. Hanging in the balance, the 2017 Women's World Cup final!
It's been driven superbly through the covers. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Fantastic shot by Veda. She prefers to go inside out over covers with the spin and lofts it nonchalantly over the infield for a boundary.
Identical to the last delivery, Verma brings her bat down just in time to keep it out.
Sushma Verma is out next to bat.

OUT! Punam Raut is given lbw! Shrubsole with the wicket. This final is not done yet. Full length ball on off, angling in, Raut tries playing across the line but misses and is rapped on the pads. She is rapped on the front pad, they appeal and the umpire agrees. Raut has a chat with her partner and then takes the referral. But the umpire tells her that time is up. End of an excellent knock by Raut.
Huge shout for an lbw, up goes the finger. Punam Raut consults her partner and then signals for the DRS. Hang on, she has been timed out.
Full and angling into the batsman, Veda tries to flick but gets a leading edge to short third man. A single taken.
A leg cutter outside off, extra bounce, Veda pushes inside the line and misses.
50-run stand between Raut and Krishnamurthy!
FOUR! Superb shot! Veda spots that mid off is up and goes over the fielder. Latches onto a full ball in her half and nails it to the boundary. This could be the big over that India needed.

FOUR! Up and over! Vital boundary this for India. Width on offer outside off, Veda makes space and spoons it over point for a boundary. No fielder in the deep square on the off side. Good choice of placement.
Anya Shrubsole returns in the attack. 47 needed off 48 balls.
Plenty of risk involved in that shot. Veda once again plays a late cut, almost off the off stump and gets it away wide of short third man. A single taken.
Bowls a full toss on off, Veda dances down the track and pushes it on one bounce straight to the cover fielder.
Nearly bowled! An arm ball around leg, Veda moves back to play the late cut but misses. It almost kissed the leg stump. The English players cannot believe it.
Full floated ball on middle, a nice looking sweep shot, behind square leg and wide of short fine leg for a single.
Advances down the track and taps it down with the spin to covers. Steals a quick single.
Fullish and on off, Raut kneels and sweeps it behind square leg for a single.
51 needed from 54 balls. Alex Hartley is brought back into the attack.
A late cut again, this time by Punam, the point fielder fielder dives to stop the ball and they cross for a run. 10-1-40-0, Marsh is done for the evening.
Spinning back into the batsman from around off, Raut closes the face of the bat and helps it to mid-wicket.
In the air... safe! Loopy off spinner on off, Raut top edges her slog sweep over short fine leg and collects a couple of runs.
Full floated ball on off, driven off the front foot to cover-point.
Flighted and on middle, Veda moves back and plays a late cut towards short third man for a single.
Too full in length on off, Punam pushes it with an angled bat to point and rushes across to the other end. Struggling with her calf but still putting in all with the title on the line.

Full outside off, Raut goes inside out and lofts it over the covers. Katherine Brunt is the one doing the chasing and she does well by stopping it just inside the rope. However, as she's getting up to throw it back in, she slightly twists her left ankle so parries it to the other fielder. The Indian batters take three runs amidst all this.
Fuller length delivery outside off, Veda lofts it over extra cover. There is a fielder out there at wide long off who comes across to her left and cuts it off. Just a run to the total.
As she's done most of the day, Raut waits for it and dabs it towards point. Single taken.
Sliding in on leg, looks to whip it away but it goes off her pads fine down the leg side. A leg bye taken.
Length delivery angling in on middle and off, Krishnamurthy meets it with a straight bat in defense.
Full and slow, on the pads, lofted over mid-wicket towards the fielder in the deep for a comfortable single.

This slight halt in play is due to a cramp suffered by Punam Raut. She is down on the ground as the physio attends to her left calf, is getting some fluids in and doing her stretches. Back on her feet, good to go...
Stays back deep inside her crease and keeps it out off the back foot. Does so rather comfortably too.
Marsh with some decent flight on this, tosses it up outside off, Punam Raut skips out and knocks it to long on for a single.
Worked away to mid-wicket with a closed face.
Defended off the front foot by the batter presenting the full face of the bat.
Appeal for a leg before, that was never going to be given though. Impact was way outside off. Raut went across to defend a full ball but it went off her pad.
Full and straight, hit firmly straight to mid-wicket.
Quick single taken. Raut dabs this short ball in front of point and sets off. Slight hesitation between the two batters but they complete the run with ease in the end.
Drives this full delivery down to long off and gets off strike.
Quite full in length, Veda is half-forward in defense.
Flat and outside off, a gentle push from Veda on the off side.

Dropped! Heather Knight the culprit, of all the people. Is that the match? Veda Krishnamurthy looks to drive along the ground but ends up chipping it towards the England captain at short extra cover. She moves to her right, it's flying into her hands and then just pops out. Just like that. She knows what a big mistake that is.
Full outside off, driven between cover-point and point. The fielder from cover-point dives to her left and manages to get a hand to it, thereby taking some pace off the ball. The batters take two.
Hangs back and keeps it out from the back foot.
On the leg stump line, picked off the hips to the leg side for a run.
Keeps somewhat low as it goes off the surface, Punam crouches a bit herself as she clips it to mid-wicket for one run.
Turning in, Raut moves inside the line and works it away on the on side.
FOUR! Uses the pace of the bowler well here. Deft, clever stuff from Punam Raut. Short and wide, just waits for this one to come and dabs it wide of short third man for a boundary.
Fuller length ball outside off, a gentle push from Raut to the cover fielder.
Fullish outside off, pushed to the covers for nothing.
Wide! Down the leg side, wide called by the umpire.

FOUR! No stopping that one, not a chance. Krishnamurthy adjusts well and drives it between mid off and extra cover. The fielder tries chasing it down but it's rolling down the slope and eventually goes away to the boundary line.
Flat and short outside off, punched off the back foot with a straight bat.

That's a fantastic effort from Jenny Gunn. Veda charges out and hammers it over the bowler's head. Seems the ball will go across the rope but Gunn comes running across to her left from long on and puts in a full stretch dive to keep it inside the rope. Terrific fielding. Keeps the batters to just two.
Brings out the broom. It's dropped on a driving length, Raut sweeps it through backward square leg for a single.
Spinning down leg, Punam uses that well and just tickles it fine. Picks up a couple of runs for doing so.
Batting Powerplay signalled.
Punam plays a sweep shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.

Sarah Taylor has missed a stumping! You read that right, but not entirely her fault though. Was a difficult take. Raut steps out to play but completely misjudges the length and the sharp turn. Goes right through her and to Taylor, who fails to gather it as he probably doesn't see it till the last second.
Works it around her front pad on the leg side for one.
FOUR! Takes the safest route to fetch herself a boundary. Krishnamurthy charges out and clobbers it straight back over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Raut gets to the pitch of the ball and connects. One run added to the total.
Fuller delivery outside off, blocked out off the front foot.
Laura Marsh is back into the attack.
Veda comes out and looks to block, takes it on the pads but she's too far out to be given out. Impact was probably what saved her but maybe she was too much down the track.

Loopy delivery spinning away from around off, Krishnamurthy drives it to the left of short cover. Heather Knight there doesn't let it go past her as she dives full stretch to stop it. Excellent effort.
Darted around leg, swept down to short fine leg.

Drinks taken. England will be taking a huge sigh of relief now after breaking the stubborn stand between Kaur and Raut. They have got rid of the dangerous Harmanpreet and now would like to apply pressure. India will hope for another partnership here. 91 needed from 99 balls. Out walks, Veda Krishnamurthy to accompany Raut.

OUT! GONE! KAUR IS OUT OF HERE! England have struck gold at a crucial juncture. Can the hosts come back into this game now? Fuller on middle and leg, Kaur gets down on one knee and sweeps it over backward square leg. A meter here or there and she would have found the boundary. But instead, finds Tammy Beaumont out in the deep. Crushing blow to India, lost their star hitter at the wrong time.
Driven through mid off to the fielder in the deep. A run is taken.
Comes down the track but isn't quite close to the pitch, somehow still manages to long on for a single.
Sliding in on leg, catching Punam high on the thigh pad as she looks to put bat on ball.
10th ODI fifty for Harmanpreet Kaur.

Fifty for Kaur! Short ball which is pulled towards fine leg. Gets to her milestone with that. Played a gem in the semis, doing the same here today in the final. Though, the nature of both knocks are so contrasting.
Full ball attacking the stumps, driven to mid on for nothing.
Turns this through backward square leg and jogs across.

How close was that? Punam Raut could have just as easily been out of here. Slow full toss around leg, angling down, Raut with a wild whip which she misses. Hits her front pad first before hitting the back one. Lucky here, the first impact saved her. Was going down leg at that point.
Full length delivery on middle, Harmanpreet slogs it hard off the inner hald through mid-wicket for a single.
Loopy, slow and pitched full outside off, Raut looks to drive it with the spin but is beaten past the outside edge. India need 96 to win off 108 deliveries.
Walks down the wicket and hammers it down the ground for an easy run.
Looped up outside off, comes ahead and blocks it out.
Flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.

FOUR! That's a fantastic shot. Beautiful use of the feet and she picked her spot well. Gave the charge, went inside out and bisected the gap between extra cover and mid off for a boundary. The target is less than 100 runs away now.

Run out chance missed! Raut taps this to covers and Kaur is off. She's instantly sent back as the fielder has a shy at the bowler's end. Misses but had that hit, she would have been in trouble. Survived a close call, there.
Alex Hartley comes into the attack.

Seemed like a wide but nothing from the umpire. Sliding down, Kaur looks to sweep but misses. Shouts of a leg before turned down. The umpire thinks there must be some pad on it, otherwise there's no other reason not to signal a wide.
Outside off again, another dab from Raut. This time to the right of short third man. Quick single taken.
Well wide outside off, Punam dabs it to short third man and both batters take a quick run. The throw is wayward and this allows the Indian pair to come back for the second.
Full and straight, driven down to long on for one.
Length delivery outside off, Punam plays this late. Waits for it and then dabs it down towards third man for a single.
Raut moves inside the line and tucks it through backward square leg. Runs the first one hard and easily manages to come back for the second. Good running.
Katherine Brunt is called back on for a bowl.
10th ODI fifty for Punam Raut!
On middle, Raut quietly helps it in the gap at mid-wicket for one. Handy knock this from the little lady. She needs to carry on though. 109 needed off 120 balls.
Strides forward to a full ball and eases it down to long on for a single.
Length ball on off, Kaur pushes it straight to covers. The fielder fires the throw to the keeper who fumbles but no run taken.
Full again, on middle, forced down to long on for a single.
Full in length outside off, Punam takes a calculative risk and lofts it over extra cover for a couple of runs.
Around leg on a length, Raut fails to flick and it brushes her pads. Rolls to short fine leg and they pick up a leg bye.
Length delivery angling into the batsman, Raut taps it down to point and looks for a run. Kaur is not interested.
Short and on middle, angling down, pulled down to long leg for a single.

FOUR! Nearly a wicket there. Straighter delivery, on middle around fuller length, Kaur gets across with the flick shot and it takes the inner half of the bat. Races down to fine leg for a boundary. Had she missed that, she was dead plumb.
Works a full ball on the leg side but finds mid-wicket.

Slower delivery, full and outside off, Kaur opens the face of the bat and pushes it towards short third man. Wants the run but Raut sends her back quickly. Harmanpreet is not impressed and gives a stare to her partner.
Full length ball angling down the leg side, Punam fails to flick and it goes off her pads to fine leg. They cross for a leg bye.
Angling a length ball on middle, Harmanpreet works it on the leg side but straight to mid-wicket.
Soft hands. Taps a length ball down in front of backward point and pinches a single.
Very full in length on middle, driven straight down the ground, just past the stumps at the other end. The long on fielder cut it off and they crossed for a single.
Pitches it on the fuller length outside off, it's pushed off the front foot to extra cover.
Fullish and around off, Kaur presses forward and defends.
Good length ball on middle, defended off the back foot.
Anya Shrubsole is back on. England need wickets now. 123 needed off 138 balls.
Very full and on the pads, pushed with soft hands to mid-wicket for one.
FOUR! Welcome boundary for India! Poor delivery, short and straight, Harmanpreet turns inside the crease and eases it all along the ground to the long leg boundary.
On a length and outside off, tapped down to short third man where the fielder made a tumbling stop. A single taken.
Fullish and outside off, driven square of the wicket on the off side but straight to backward point.
Angling down the leg side, Punam tries to flick but closes the face of the bat early. It pops out off the leading edge but drops safely near her partner.
Straighter delivery, on a length and extra bounce, Kaur does well to work it in front of square leg for a single. 100 up for India!
Edgy! Full toss outside off, Raut tries to drive through covers but it catches the outside edge and runs down to third man. Laura Marsh chases it down and they take a brace.
Up and over the infield. Width on offer outside off, Punam stays back and lifts it over extra cover for a couple of runs.
Free Hit time...
No ball called for above the waist high full toss. It's pushed from the crease to covers.
Once again uses her feet and this time bunts it down to long on for a single.
Full and wide outside off, Harmanpreet dances down the track and drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Around off on a length, punched back to the bowler.
50-run stand between Kaur and Raut!
Wicket to wicket line, fuller in length, it's helped in front of square leg for a single.
Skipper Heather Knight brings herself into the attack.
Driven towards the long on region. They pick up a single.
On a length outside off, tapped down to point with an angled bat.

Shout for an lbw! Not given. Heather Knight has a chat with Sarah Taylor and decides not to take the DRS. Full length ball angling into the batsman from around off, Raut fails to flick from the crease and is hit on the pads. They put in an unsuccessful appeal. Missing leg, confirms the Ball Tracker.
Slow dipping delivery, full and on middle, it's worked through mid-wicket for one.
Full and on middle, angling down, Raut sits down on one knee and paddles it over the keeper's head. A single taken.
Length ball slipping down the leg side, Kaur deflects it off his pads to fine leg for a single.
Natalie Sciver returns to bowl.
Reverts to using the feet, dances down the track and forces it down the ground to long on for one.

SIX! High and handsome! This will ease off some pressure. No use of the feet this time, a big stride forward instead with a big backlift. Kaur launches it in front of square leg for a biggie. The fielder in the deep mid-wicket region runs across to her right but it goes well over.
Flatter this time, full and around leg, it's swept behind square leg for one.
Once again Kaur gets down the track and nudges it off the inner portion of the bat past mid-wicket. A single taken.
Strides forward to a full ball and plays it straight to mid-wicket.
Floated ball, full and drifting in around off, Harmanpreet skips down the track and drives it firmly to sweeper cover.
Another charge down the track from the batter but this time she finds the short mid-wicket fielder.
Swift use of the feet by Kaur as he comes down the track and eases a full ball to long on. A single to keep the scoreboard ticking.
Spinning down the leg side, the batsman fails to play the paddle sweep and the keeper also fumbles. It goes off her gloves to short fine leg and they cross. Given as a run. Hmm...
Jumps out of the crease again but makes the length very fuller to make any use of it. Digs it out to mid-wicket.
Nicely tossed up delivery, full and on off, knocked down to long on for another single.
Runs down the track and flicks it with the spin to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up ball, around leg, Kaur comes down the track for a big shot but nearly yorks herself. Does well in the end to keep it out.
Very full and on middle, swept in front of square leg for one.
Slower delivery, outside off, Punam taps it down to point.
Walks down the track to a shortish ball and smashes it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Miscommunication! Floated full ball on off, Harmanpreet gets forward and defends it off the inside edge to mid-wicket. Raut looks for a run and comes running down, sent back by Kaur in time.
Too full in length on off, worked across the line and the short mid-wicket fielder intervened with a dive to prevent the single.
Kaur was winding up for the big one, so Marsh darted it quick and full. The batter could only manage to drill it to long on for a run.
Drops it shorter in length, Punam is back to tap it to the covers. Takes a quick single for doing so.
Shuffles across to this full ball and wrists it to the long on fielder for one.
Spinning into Kaur, she's back to turn it 'round the corner. Wants the single initially but then decides against it seeing the fielder get to it quickly.
Raut hangs back and dabs it towards backward point. The run is on and Harmanpreet has to dive to make it in at the striker's end. Nicely done.
Quicker one well outside off from Marsh, pushed away square into the off side.

SIX! There she goes! Blocked a lot of deliveries, saw the opportunity to go for it and smoked it. Kaur used her feet to get to the pitch and slogged it over mid-wicket for a maximum. 10 runs from the over!
Flicked away against the turn on the on side for one run.
Stays right back to this flat ball and punches it out off the back foot.

Floated around leg, Raut kneels down and plays the paddle. The keeper, Taylor, moves to her left and tries to catch it, premeditating that shot from the batter. Misses though as it goes over her head. A couple added to the scoreboard.
Pushed through the gap in the covers for an easy single.
Flights it up outside off, gets right to the pitch and blocks.
Makes good use of her feet to get to the pitch of the delivery and pushes it past the diving bowler for a run.
Wide! Fires it down the leg side, Kaur looks to help it on its way but fails to do so.
Unable to find the gap again. It's worked across the line straight to short mid-wicket.
The batter gets to the pitch of the ball and decides to defend it.
With a little shimmy down the wicket, Punam Raut gets close to the pitch and wrists it to long on. Single taken.
Jumps down the wicket and finds the gap in the mid-wicket area for one.
Looped up delivery just outside off, defended back down the track with a straight bat.
Quicker through the air, on middle and leg, swept away through square leg for a single.
Comes half-forward and deals with it well.
With an authoritative walk, Kaur comes down the track and pushes it towards mid off, where Heather Knight tumbles to her right to stop it.
Turning ever so slightly from around off, Harmanpreet gets behind the line to block.
Very full again, Kaur drills it straight to the fielder at mid on.
Starts from around the wicket and bowls a good tossed up delivery. Nice drift into the batter on a full length, it's kept out back down the track.
Alex Hartley is introduced into the attack.

That slight halt in play has allowed the umpires to call for drinks! England are bowling well here, keeping the pressure and not leaking many runs. Have scalped two wickets, including the one of the Indian skipper. This current Indian pair need to play on for a decent amount of time now, otherwise there will be a lot of pressure on the Women in Blue.

Flighted on a driving length, Raut reaches out and drives it square through point. Two fielders chase it down and keep it inside the rope with good team work. Two runs taken. Seems Raut has a cramp or some kind of minor injury, so the physio is out. We have a slight halt in play.
Darted pretty full, driven back down the ground for a single.
Harmanpreet has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Marsh with a lot of revolutions on this occasion, Kaur drives it straight to short cover.
Loopy and dipping in outside off, Punam makes good use of her feet and flicks it wide of mid on for a single.
Tossed up on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Good effort from the skipper, saved vital runs for her side. Kaur drove it to the left of cover where Heather Knight was positioned, she dived to her left and made a good stop.
Plants her front foot forward and defends it with the full face of the bat.
Full ball quite straight in line, driven to mid on.
Fuller again, the batter is forward and across to push it to mid off.
Short of a good length outside off, Harmanpreet offers a solid punch straight to the mid off fielder.
Tight line on off, blocked away into the off side.
Shout for an lbw! Turned down. It's dropped short, flat and turning in from outside off, Raut leans across to play at it but is caught on the thigh pad. Impact was outside leg, that saved her.
Flat and short, punched down to long on by Kaur for a run.
Full and straight from Laura Marsh, it's driven straight back to her.
FOUR! Harmanpreet walks down the track and takes this one on the full. Doesn't connect well but just about manages to clear mid on. Goes over the fielder there and races away to the boundary line.
Driven to the covers for another dot ball.
Goes across to this one and works it away on the leg side.
On the fifth stump line, pushed to the cover area, straight to the fielder.
Off cutter from Jenny Gunn, Harmanpreet flicks it off her pads and works it to backward square leg for a quick one.
Seaming off the deck and coming back in, worked away to mid-wicket. No run taken.
Quite close to off, Kaur is half-forward as she meets it with a straight bat.
Tight line, not offering any room to Harmanpreet Kaur as she can only get behind the line and defends.
Good length delivery well outside off, run down to third man with an open face for one.
Presents a tight defensive shot to see the over out. A successful one from Laura Marsh.
Another ball, another drive to the same region.
Full again, a bit straight in line as Harmanpreet drives to mid on.
Kaur has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and straight on middle, Kaur brings her bat in front of her pad and defends.
Harmanpreet Kaur is the new batsman. He is fresh from a sensational knock against Australia in the semis. India need her to stand up and perform again.

OUT! BIG WICKET FOR ENGLAND! The crowd at Lord's erupts at the Indian captain is dismissed, they know how important that wicket is. Raut works it to mid-wicket and sets off for the run. Natalie Sciver is the fielder there and she's lighting quick to get to the ball. Throws is quickly at the keeper who whips the bails off. Looks like Raj is gone, but it's taken upstairs. Replays show she's well short. Strange piece of running from her, in her last World Cup, she showed no urgency to get in. Didn't stretch her bat out, put no dive in. Didn't seem that interested at all. England won't mind that though, not at all.
Laura Marsh to bowl her off spinners.
Another full ball, another drive from Raj to mid on.
Mithali is well forward to this full delivery as she drives it to mid on.
Good, alert running. Raut drops it in front of cover and takes off. The fielder gets to the ball and ends up missing her shy at the bowler's end. Completed with ease in the end.
Fuller in length, outside off. Makes Mithali reach for it and she drives it through the covers for a run.
On a length again, comfortably outside off this time, meets it with the full face of the bat.
Angling in on off, on a length, Mithali Raj hangs back and punches it towards wide mid on.
On the fuller side of the length, kept out by coming half-forward with a straight bat.
Coming back in on middle and leg, clipped behind square leg for a run.

FOUR! Beautiful shot from the Indian skipper. Great balance as she plays that. Fuller in length, she drives it a bit square through cover-point for a boundary. Super timing on that, opened the bat face slightly and put it away.
Brings his skillful wrists into play this time, turns it through mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! Seems Punam Raut wants to be in the headline tomorrow. She's really going for it. Cross seam delivery on the stumps, on a full length, Raut kneels down and slogs it comfortably over mid-wicket. Clears the infield and earns herself a boundary.
Short of a good length outside off, Raut moves across and taps it down right beside her on the off side.
Back-to-back maidens for England! Mithali gets forward to a length ball and defends it towards cover.
Excellent pressure being built by the English bowlers, 11 dots in a row now. Length ball outside off, Mithali presses forward to block well.
Length ball wider outside off, reaches out and defends firmly towards cover.
On middle and leg, Raj gets across and clips it towards the leg side.
Good shot but no run! Fullish outside off, leans forward and drives but straight to cover-point.
Full and outside off, leans forward and blocks it towards cover.
Jenny Gunn is introduced into the attack.
Maiden to start for Sciver! Length ball outside off, gets on the front foot and taps it gently towards point.
Shortish length on off stump, tapped gently towards short mid-wicket by riding the bounce. Tight over this from Sciver.
On a good length around middle, Raut flicks neatly but cannot beat the fielder at square leg.
Length ball outside off, defended solidly from the crease towards short cover.
Back of a length around off, Punam hangs back and defends it towards short mid-wicket.
On a length on off stump, stays back and blocks with the full face of the bat.
Natalie Sciver is into the bowling attack now.
On a shortish length outside off, Mithali stays back and defends firmly to the off side.
On a length outside off, waits for it and glides gently to third man for a single.
Length ball on off stump, Raut gets a faint inside edge onto the pads.

SIX! BANG BANG! Raut is in an attacking mood today, folks. Fuller ball around off stump, in the slot and she clobbers it over the bowler's head by going down on one knee. Terrific connection and clears the long on fence. Such an effortless shot!
Full and outside off, leans forward and defends it towards cover.
Uppish but safe! Length ball around middle, gets across and checks the flick stroke. Nearly carries towards short mid-wicket.
Length ball outside off, stands tall and taps it towards point.
Fullish ball outside off, Mithali leans into it and defends it to the off side.
Length ball outside off, gets back and taps it towards backward point.
Full and outside off, defended solidly off the front foot to the off side.
Length ball outside off, Raj leans forward and blocks it to the off side.

FOUR! Poor ball and punished! Full toss on the pads, Raj duly clips it off her pads through mid-wicket. Sublime shot and the ball races away to the fence. It was there to be put away but the execution was classy. With this, Mithali Raj has completed 400 runs in this tournament. She becomes only the third captain to score 400-plus runs in a single edition of the Women's World Cup.
Length ball around off, gets across and pats it down the track to the bowler.
Fullish and outside off, Raut drives sweetly towards cover-point.
On a length outside off, blocked solidly towards the point fielder.
Pitched up outside off, Raut gets forward and checks her drive to short cover.
Fullish on middle and leg, gets across and clips it through backward square leg as the fine leg fielder tidies up. Single taken. A second run was on there but no intent.
On a shortish length outside off, gets back and dabs it down to third man for a single.

FOUR! All class! Slightly short and wide outside off, Mithali delays the glide to beat the backward point fielder. Beautifully timed and the ball races to the fence for a boundary. Third man had no chance of stopping it.
Fuller ball outside off, gets on the front foot and defends gently to short cover.
Just on a length around off stump, solidly defended with a straight bat from Mithali. Solid as ever!
Back of a length outside off, Mithali rocks back and taps it towards the point fielder.
The rain has gotten heavier now. The crowd has brought out its umbrellas and raincoats.
On a length outside off, stands tall and pushes it towards point.
Back of a length outside off, width on offer and cut away through backward point. The fielder at third man gets across to her right to tidy up as a single is taken.
Fuller and outside off, Mithali gets forward and pats it towards cover where there is a fumble. They thought of the single but then decided against it.
As predicted, it has started to drizzle. Hopefully it's just a passing shower.
Good length closer to off stump, defended solidly off the front foot by Mithali.
Shortish in length this time outside off, steered through backward point for a single.
FOUR! UP AND OVER! How's that for confidence! Fullish around off, Punam leans into it and lofts it cleanly over the bowler's head. Easily clears mid on to find the fence. Good intent from the opener!
Back of a length outside off, punched solidly off the back foot towards point.
Fullish and outside off, presses forward and defends solidly towards cover.
Length ball on fifth stump channel, left alone by Raj.
Shortish and well wide outside off, Punam reaches out and steers it down to third man for a run.
Fullish and outside off, Punam pushes with hard hands at it but only manages a thick inside edge on to the pads.
On a length wider outside off, left alone to the keeper.
Length ball closer to off stump, defended solidly from the crease towards short cover.
Back of a length wider outside off, Mithali opens the bat face to run it down to third man. Single added to the total.
Fuller and outside off, pushed gently back to the bowler. Successful over for England.
Full and around middle, swinging in, sharp inward movement but Mithali gets her bat around the front pad just in time. Chops it down to fine leg for a single. The captain is away.
Mithali Raj walks in next at number 3.

OUT! Those wides are made up for. What a delivery! Ideal early breakthrough for Anya Shrubsole. Bowls it on a length, it's going on straight, not much movement on it. Mandhana is forward to defend but not forward enough. The ball goes past her hanging bat and knocks the stumps over. Mandhana wasn't looking very assured, now departs via a tentative defensive shot. The left-hander made an incredible start to the tournament, 196 in her first two matches but then her woes started and continued as he managed only 36 in her next seven.
Wide! Down the leg side again, wide called. Shrubsole is struggling with her line here.
Length delivery aiming the off bail, Mandhana hangs back to punch it on the off side but gets an inside edge onto her pads.
Wide! Way down the leg side, Smriti with an attempted glance behind square on the leg side, ends up missing it.
Slightly fullish in length, around off, driven to mid off by Mandhana from within her crease.
Too straight in line, nudged down to fine leg for one.
Wide! Bit of a false start from Shrubsole. She slips it down the leg side, Raut looks to flick but misses.
Anya Shrubsole to bowl from the other end. A slip in place.
Length delivery around off, driven to mid off on the up to end a good first over from Katherine Brunt.
Short of a good length outside off, Punam Raut goes back and runs it down to third man with an open face. She and India are off the mark.
Fraction ahead of a length, kept out solidly off the front foot.
In the channel outside off, on a good length, Punam Raut withdraws her bat and watches as the ball goes past her. Not much bounce on this occasion, that one kept quite low.
Fullish in length, outside the line of off stump, Raut pushes it straight to the fielder at cover.
Good length delivery just outside off, Raut takes a good stride forward and blocks it in front of covers.

We are back for the run chase. It's for the big prize here, India need 229 to become world champions for the first time in history. England need to defend the same to become winners for the fourth time. The hosts are in a huddle and are now spreading out across the field. Smriti Mandhana and Punam Raut will open the pressure innings, with Katherine Brunt to take the new ball first up. A slip in place for her. For the World Cup, here we go...
